protocol.name: acompositor_inject_v1

description.summary: input from a remote desktop, as evdev codes

protocol.description: A remote desktop process feeds the keyboard and pointer of whoever sits at the other end into acompositor, as if they came from local devices: they go through the same shortcuts, focus rules, input method grab and lock screen as local input. Keys and buttons are evdev codes (KEY_*, BTN_*), so no keymap is involved. Only connections the session handed over at the remote level are offered this global.

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: a state that is neither released nor pressed

entry.name: invalid_code
entry.summary: a key or button code outside 1..=767

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: a screen size of 0 or above 8192 pixels

description.summary: stop injecting; keys and buttons still held are released

request.name: key

description.summary: press or release a keyboard key

request.description: key is an evdev KEY_* code; a press of a key already held is ignored, as is a release of a key that is not held.

request.name: button

description.summary: press or release a pointer button

request.description: button is an evdev BTN_* code, such as BTN_LEFT (0x110).

request.name: move_by

description.summary: move the pointer relative to where it is

request.description: dx and dy are logical pixels, as from a mouse.

request.name: move_to

description.summary: move the pointer to a place on the screens

request.description: x and y are logical coordinates in the compositor's space, the same as wl_output.geometry and xdg-output; the pointer stays on the screens.

request.name: wheel

description.summary: turn the wheel by whole detents

request.description: Signs as evdev: horizontal right is positive, vertical away from the user is positive.

request.name: scroll

description.summary: smooth scrolling, as from two fingers

request.description: dx and dy are logical pixels of content movement, as wl_pointer.axis values; send scroll_stop when the fingers lift.

request.name: text
request.description: Printable ASCII, newline and tab are typed as key presses on acompositor's US layout, with shift where needed, so they go through the same paths as any key. Other characters are committed in runs to the focused client's text-input-v3 when it is enabled; when it is not, they are left out and text_skipped says how many.

description.summary: characters of the last text request that could not be typed

request.name: drop

description.summary: drop data on the surface at a place, as if dragged there

request.description: source is a wl_data_source of this client that already offers its types (for files, text/uri-list). acompositor moves the pointer to x, y in the compositor's logical space and drags the source onto the surface there; once that surface accepts a type (and, between version 3 sides, an action) the drop happens, and if it refuses or says nothing within a second the drag is cancelled. The source hears the outcome as in any drag: send, dnd_drop_performed and dnd_finished, or cancelled.

description.summary: the end of a smooth scroll

request.name: resize_screen

description.summary: ask for a headless screen of this size

request.description: When the remote client's window changes size, ask for the screen to follow, in physical pixels. Only a headless acompositor (--headless) obeys; on real screens the request is ignored. Clients see the new size through wl_output, maximized windows refill the new work area, and capture sessions get new buffer constraints.

request.name: target

description.summary: send the Agent's input into one window

request.description: Only for Agent-level and dev-level connections; others are ignored. identifier is a toplevel's acompositor_window_v1.identifier (acompositor-N); an empty string ends the targeting. While a window is targeted, move_to takes x and y in that window's logical coordinates (its geometry's top left is 0, 0) and the pointer only hits that window, its subsurfaces and its popups. Keys go to that window's client: when the person's keyboard is elsewhere, the client is lent the keyboard (wl_keyboard enter, key, modifiers) without moving the person's focus, as the Agent's pointer is lent. A window on the Agent's stage is never raised or focused by this input and nothing of the person's changes. A window on the person's desktops behaves as before: a press raises it and gives it the keyboard, and keys first focus it. When the window is not found or later closes, target_lost is sent once and the input is dropped until the next target.

description.summary: the targeted window is gone; input is dropped until the next target

request.name: focus_desktop

description.summary: give the keyboard to the desktop, as a click on it would

request.description: Only for dev-level connections; others are ignored, and so is the request while the screen is locked. The desktop is the background-layer panel that takes the keyboard on demand; it gets the keyboard focus as if the person had clicked on it, until a window is activated or clicked. With no such panel nothing happens.
